interest: This document provides a fascinating glimpse into Japanese covert diplomacy and naval maneuvering in Latin America during World War II, specifically Tokyo's efforts to keep Chile neutral following the Rio Conference of 1942. It highlights intelligence regarding the activities of Japanese Secret Service operative Sozan Miyoshi and his audacious proposal to stage a naval show of force by sending four or five warships to Chilean ports conditioned on securing local fuel oil supplies for their return. For diplomatic and intelligence historians, it illustrates both Axis efforts to influence South American neutrality and the acute fuel constraints dictating Japanese naval operations in the Pacific.
overview: This file consists of a single State Department cross-reference sheet (decimal file 894.3325/1) dated November 14, 1942, referring to a confidential memorandum from the War Department filed under 740.0011 Pacific War/3020. The document records intelligence that Japanese Secret Service agent Sozan Miyoshi informed Chilean officials that four or five Japanese warships could visit Chile if fuel oil were provided for their return voyage. The reported initiative was viewed by U.S. officials as an attempt by Japan to influence Chile to maintain its diplomatic neutrality during World War II.

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet noting intelligence that Japanese agent Sozan Miyoshi offered to arrange a visit of Japanese warships to Chile if provided with fuel oil to help keep Chile neutral.
subfiles.summary: This State Department cross-reference sheet indexes a confidential War Department memorandum dated November 14, 1942, classified under decimal file 740.0011 Pacific War/3020. It records that Japanese Secret Service agent Sozan Miyoshi reportedly approached Chilean officials with an offer to arrange a visit of four or five Japanese warships to Chile, contingent upon receiving fuel oil for their return voyage. The overture was evaluated as an effort to persuade Chile to maintain its diplomatic neutrality during the Pacific War.
